title: The Doorman's Fallacy in action
summary: An essay discussing 'The Doorman's Fallacy' - a cognitive bias or logical error where someone incorrectly attributes causation or significance to a particular gatekeeping moment or threshold, often observed in gatekeeping scenarios where doormen or bouncers believe their actions determine outcomes that would occur regardless.
problem_solved: Examines a common logical fallacy where gatekeepers overestimate their causal role in filtering outcomes
why_valuable: Helps readers recognize when authority figures mistakenly believe their decisions are more consequential than they actually are
